simulations.title: Investigate a training portal outage
simulations.context: A fictional course portal becomes unreliable after a change. Examine a synthetic timeline and prepare a reasoned conclusion.
evidence: 10:00 portal HTTP errors rise from 1% to 28%
10:02 deployment release 2.1 completed
10:04 authentication service healthy; database latency elevated
10:09 rollback to release 2.0 began
10:15 errors fall to 2%; full verification pending
steps: The newest release is proven to be the sole cause
The error-rate increase is measured. Root cause needs verification.
The deployment or its dependencies may affect service health
A plausible temporal relationship is a hypothesis, not proof.
Compare deployment changes, dependency metrics and approved tests
Use scoped evidence and reversible procedures.
Exercise key student workflows and observe stable service health
simulations.memoPrompt: Write a 150–250 word incident note: confirmed facts, competing hypotheses, decision taken, and verification plan.

simulations.title: Review enterprise access permissions
simulations.context: A fictional employee transfers from payroll to customer support. Their old payroll-editor group remains assigned.
evidence: Policy: support personnel may read customer cases
Identity audit: user still in payroll-editors
Payroll activity audit: no edits confirmed in reviewed period
HR record: department change approved three weeks ago
steps: The assignment conflicts with current role requirements.
Effective privileges and review of approved access changes
A list of private customer passwords
Actual effective permissions and lifecycle records help quantify risk.
Revoke unneeded group membership through approved workflow
Verify effective access for permitted and denied actions
Assume no risk because no edits were logged
simulations.memoPrompt: Write a 150–250 word access review: policy deviation, evidence, risk, remedy and validation.

simulations.title: Analyze a small network failure
simulations.context: A fictional office workstation can reach its gateway but cannot access a named training site.
evidence: Gateway ping: replies received
Approved remote IP connectivity: works
DNS lookup for training.example.test: failed
Other workstation on same network resolves the name
steps: Name resolution is failing while other IP connectivity works.
What hypothesis is consistent with the evidence?
Device-specific resolver configuration or cache problem
Comparison with another workstation narrows the problem.
Which diagnostic step is least disruptive?
Inspect assigned resolvers and error responses
Start with reversible tests on authorized devices.
The name resolves and the original application workflow succeeds
Validate name resolution and actual functionality.
simulations.memoPrompt: Write a 150–250 word help-desk escalation including symptoms, observations, hypothesis, next check and success criterion.

simulations.title: Assess a simulated web privacy boundary
simulations.context: A fictional learning service serves private grades through a backend API. A test student uses a supplied synthetic record.
evidence: Policy: students may see only their own grades
UI hides other students' grade links
Synthetic API test: GET /grades/student-b using student-a token returns 200
Response is synthetic, with no real data
Owner: course platform engineering
steps: Backend authorization may not enforce record ownership
Client visibility does not replace server record checks.
What does the synthetic 200 response demonstrate?
A policy mismatch in the scoped lab test
That all production endpoints behave identically
The test establishes only the observed synthetic environment behavior.
Authorize each requested record on the trusted backend
Enforce the policy on the server or database security layer.
Verify both owned-record access and denial of other records
Test positive and negative cases with authorized synthetic accounts.
simulations.memoPrompt: Write a 150–250 word security finding with scope, observation, impact, remediation and retest.
